datasets.scope_note: Every truck the Chamber recorded entering Gaza, commercial and humanitarian, all crossings, by week; looted and delivered trucks for the weeks a report states them. Weeks of March to mid-May 2025 are zero by the reports' own sentences (the crossings closed on 2 March 2025).
warnings: Stated with the looted trucks for 18 weeks of May to September 2025 (week 43 states only the looted); with them it makes the week's trucks entered.

A week's count, dated by the week's first day (its last day is in the row): every truck the Gaza Chamber of Commerce recorded entering Gaza, commercial and humanitarian, through all crossings. The weeks of March to mid-May 2025 are zero because the reports state the crossings were closed; a zero is the report's sentence, not a missing figure. It is not UN2720's count (only UN-coordinated aid) nor UNRWA's (ended January 2025): never one series.

Stated by the reports for 19 weeks, 20 May to 28 September 2025; the other weeks have no figure, which is not zero. Looted here is the Chamber's word for trucks taken on the road or from warehouses before they reached the people or traders they were sent to.

datasets.scope_note: Only humanitarian consignments processed through the UN2720 Mechanism. Three stages of one journey (offloaded, collected, arrived): never added together. The publisher revises past days and caps the window at its last verified day.
warnings: Pallets of aid that reached their intended destination inside Gaza that day, as verified by the UN2720 Mechanism (UNOPS). It says nothing about distribution to families, and it covers only cargo sent through that UN mechanism (no commercial goods, no aid sent outside it). It is not UNRWA's count, which ended on 16 January 2025: the two are never one series.

Tonnes of aid that reached their intended destination inside Gaza that day, as verified by the UN2720 Mechanism (UNOPS). It says nothing about distribution to families, and it covers only cargo sent through that UN mechanism (no commercial goods, no aid sent outside it). It is not UNRWA's count, which ended on 16 January 2025: the two are never one series.

Trucks of aid that reached their intended destination inside Gaza that day, as verified by the UN2720 Mechanism (UNOPS). It says nothing about distribution to families, and it covers only cargo sent through that UN mechanism (no commercial goods, no aid sent outside it). It is not UNRWA's truck count, which ended on 16 January 2025: the two are never one series.

Pallets of aid picked up from a crossing that day and driven into Gaza, counted by the UN2720 Mechanism (UNOPS). Collected is not delivered: part of it was intercepted on the road before it reached its destination. It covers only cargo sent through that UN mechanism. It is not UNRWA's count, which ended on 16 January 2025: the two are never one series.

Tonnes of aid picked up from a crossing that day and driven into Gaza, counted by the UN2720 Mechanism (UNOPS). Collected is not delivered: part of it was intercepted on the road before it reached its destination. It covers only cargo sent through that UN mechanism. It is not UNRWA's count, which ended on 16 January 2025: the two are never one series.

Trucks that picked up aid from a crossing that day and drove it into Gaza, counted by the UN2720 Mechanism (UNOPS). Collected is not delivered: part of it was intercepted on the road before it reached its destination. It covers only cargo sent through that UN mechanism. These trucks are smaller than the ones that unload at the crossing, so the two truck counts do not compare. It is not UNRWA's truck count, which ended on 16 January 2025: the two are never one series.

warnings: UNRWA's log of supplies entering Gaza, one row per consignment line. By the publisher's own notice the records after 5 May 2024 are partial, and the log ends on 16 January 2025: a count for any day after 5 May 2024 is a floor, not the total, and no day after 16 January 2025 has a figure at all. datasets.scope_note: ILO's quarterly series from PCBS's Labour Force Survey, by sex and age. From 2023Q4 the survey excludes the Gaza Strip (ILO note S4:6333): those quarters are series of their own, placed in the West Bank.
warnings: ILO's quarterly figure from the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics' Labour Force Survey (ILOSTAT), dated by the quarter's first day (the quarter is in the row). A break in the series or a value ILO flags as unreliable is marked on the row (obs_status). These quarters cover the West Bank and Gaza; from the fourth quarter of 2023, when Gaza could not be surveyed, the figures are a series of their own (…_excluding_gaza).

ILO's quarterly figure from the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics' Labour Force Survey (ILOSTAT), dated by the quarter's first day (the quarter is in the row). A break in the series or a value ILO flags as unreliable is marked on the row (obs_status). From the fourth quarter of 2023 the survey excludes the Gaza Strip (ILO's note: "Geographical coverage: Excluding Gaza Strip"): this series is the West Bank's, never joined to the quarters before, which cover the West Bank and Gaza.

warnings: A PROJECTION, not a measurement: the United Nations' medium-variant projection from World Population Prospects 2024, a model's output released on 11 July 2024. It assumed a recovery that the years since have not shown: it has deaths falling from 38,937 in 2023 to 16,412 in 2026, and life expectancy at birth rising from 65.2 to 77.4 years. The UN's estimates end at 2023 (population.wpp.*); every year here, from 2024 on, is the model. The UN has announced its next revision for 11 July 2027.

datasets.scope_note: Week prices of 30 goods in Gaza's markets from 1 April 2025, each with the pre-war price the report compares it with; the weeks a table printed NA for a good; the GCPI daily from 27 May 2025, by the index's weeks from 31 January 2025 and by month from February 2025. Weeks 62-65 (October 2025) were priced for North and South apart and are not here, nor are weeks 1-35.
warnings: A week's average of the prices the Gaza Chamber of Commerce recorded in Gaza's markets, dated by the week's first day (its last day is in the row), in the unit the Chamber prices the good in; each row also carries the pre-war price the report compares it with (prewar_price). The reports price the Strip as one market from week 27 (28 January 2025); before that, and in weeks 62 to 65 (October 2025), they priced the north and the south apart, which are series of their own. Rows before week 36 state no unit: theirs is the later tables' for the same pre-war price (the row's basis says so). Not WFP's monthly retail price: never one series.

A week's average of the prices the Gaza Chamber of Commerce recorded in the northern part of the Gaza Strip, dated by the week's first day (its last day is in the row). The reports priced the north and the south apart from August 2024 to January 2025, and again in October 2025, when the north was cut off from the south. The rows state no unit: the unit is the later tables' for the same pre-war price, or, where a report's pre-war price differs and the unit is not in doubt (per kilo or litre), the report's own (the row's basis says which). Where the same report's daily table gives another average, it sits beside the figure (daily_table_average). Not WFP's monthly retail price: never one series.

The Chamber's price table printed NA for this good in these weeks, in place of a price. The reports do not define NA; their summaries say, in the same weeks, that such goods were no longer found in the markets. A week with no row here is not a week the good was found: it is a week with a price, or with no table.

A week's average of the prices the Gaza Chamber of Commerce recorded in the south of the Gaza Strip, dated by the week's first day (its last day is in the row). The reports priced the north and the south apart from August 2024 to January 2025, and again in October 2025, when the north was cut off from the south. The rows state no unit: the unit is the later tables' for the same pre-war price, or, where a report's pre-war price differs and the unit is not in doubt (per kilo or litre), the report's own (the row's basis says which). Where the same report's daily table gives another average, it sits beside the figure (daily_table_average). Not WFP's monthly retail price: never one series.

The Chamber's basket is rice 1.38 kg, vegetable oil 1.37 l, sugar 1 kg, flour 12.65 kg, tomato 3.5 kg, cucumber 3.45 kg, onion 3.5 kg, potato 2.5 kg, soap, sanitary towels, washing liquid and dishwashing liquid. Daily from 27 May 2025; 29 September to 26 October 2025 were measured for North and South apart and are not here.

The Chamber's basket is rice 1.38 kg, vegetable oil 1.37 l, sugar 1 kg, flour 12.65 kg, tomato 3.5 kg, cucumber 3.45 kg, onion 3.5 kg, potato 2.5 kg, soap, sanitary towels, washing liquid and dishwashing liquid. The Chamber's monthly value, February 2025 on. A month the newest report gives only 'up to' a day is left until a report gives it whole; where two reports print a month differently, the later report's value is held.

datasets.scope_note: Each IPC analysis since December 2023: the current period and its projection, the people and the share in phases 1 to 5 and 3 or worse, by the areas that analysis used (single governorates, combined areas, the Strip). The West Bank rows analyse nobody and are not held.
warnings: An IPC acute food insecurity analysis for the Gaza Strip (National IPC Technical Working Group, via HDX): the people estimated in each phase over the analysis's period, dated by the period's first day (its last day is in the row, with the analysis's month). Each analysis states the current period and a projection for the next. IPC's areas change between analyses, so each area is a series of its own; combined areas (the northern governorates, Deir al-Balah with Khan Younis) are never one governorate. In the May 2024 analysis the file names its combined areas "North Gaza" and "Deir Al-Balah"; their populations show they are the combined areas, and they are held as such. Phase 5 at area level is catastrophe; famine is declared for an area by IPC's Famine Review Committee.

An IPC acute food insecurity analysis for the Gaza Strip (National IPC Technical Working Group, via HDX): the people estimated in each phase over the analysis's period, dated by the period's first day (its last day is in the row, with the analysis's month). Each analysis states the current period and a projection for the next. IPC's areas change between analyses, so each area is a series of its own; combined areas (the northern governorates, Deir al-Balah with Khan Younis) are never one governorate. In the May 2024 analysis the file names its combined areas "North Gaza" and "Deir Al-Balah"; their populations show they are the combined areas, and they are held as such. Phase 5 at area level is catastrophe; famine is declared for an area by IPC's Famine Review Committee. This is the analysis's PROJECTION for the period: what IPC expected, not what it measured.

Not read: exchange rates, adverts, commentary, goods priced by the uqiya or the ratl or in packs of no stated size.
warnings: The price of this good as the Telegram channel «أسعار السوق - غزة» (@asarsook) posted it for the day: one list's price, not an average or a survey, and the channel states no method. The list named no area: it may be any of the Strip's markets. A list is dated by the day it prints, else by the post's day in Gaza. Where a list prints no unit the price is per kilo, as these lists sell produce, meat and fish (the row's basis says which); a printed range is held as its midpoint, both ends beside it (range_printed); a different price the same day sits beside the figure (other_prices_same_day). Not the Chamber's weekly average or WFP's monthly price: never one series.

It counts arrest cases, not people: a person arrested twice counts twice. Months the index does not hold as a month's report are missing, not zero (the year, half-year and two-month reports are not read as months). Where a report's title prints a different figure from its text, the text's is held and the title's sits beside it (title_says).

The Palestinian prisoner institutions' joint monthly report (the Commission of Detainees' Affairs, the Prisoners' Society, Addameer; some years Al Mezan and the Wadi Hilweh centre), as Addameer indexes it: the arrests Israeli forces made in the month, from the report's lead sentence. It counts arrest cases, not people: a person arrested twice counts twice. Months the index does not hold as a month's report are missing, not zero (the year, half-year and two-month reports are not read as months). Where a report's title prints a different figure from its text, the text's is held and the title's sits beside it (title_says). From October 2023 the reports count the West Bank, Jerusalem included, only: these months are a series of their own.
